quiz.0.question: Why is Aglianico called 'the Nebbiolo of the South'?
quiz.0.options.0: It originated in Piemonte and was brought south
quiz.0.options.1: Like Nebbiolo, it is a late-ripening, high-acid, high-tannin variety with great ageing potential
quiz.0.options.2: It has the same DNA as Nebbiolo
quiz.0.options.3: It requires the same amount of oak ageing as Barolo
quiz.0.explanation: Aglianico shares Nebbiolo's key characteristics: late ripening, powerful tannins, high acidity and exceptional longevity — making it the south's answer to the north's king.
quiz.1.question: What are Campania's three great white grapes?
quiz.1.options.0: Greco di Tufo, Fiano di Avellino, Falanghina
quiz.1.explanation: Campania's 'white trinity' — Greco di Tufo DOCG, Fiano di Avellino DOCG and Falanghina — are considered three of southern Italy's greatest white wines.
quiz.2.question: What is distinctive about Vesuvio DOC?
quiz.2.options.1: Vineyards are planted on the slopes of Mount Vesuvius on volcanic soil
quiz.2.options.3: It is made exclusively from Aglianico
quiz.2.explanation: Vesuvio DOC (which includes the historic Lacryma Christi sub-zone) is grown on the volcanic slopes of Mount Vesuvius — giving wines a unique mineral and smoky character.
quiz.3.question: What is the minimum ageing requirement for Taurasi DOCG?
quiz.3.explanation: Taurasi DOCG requires a minimum of 3 years total ageing (at least 1 year in oak). Riserva requires 4 years — rivalling Barolo and Brunello in its demands.
